findings.evidence: dom-1440.json: alt="See you next week." (the subject line). The image contains all of the email's information: 'Action packed. WWDC24 June 10–14', 'Watch the keynote. Monday, June 10, at 10:00 a.m. PT. Streaming from Apple Park on apple.com.', 'Add to calendar', the legal footer. A screen-reader user gets only the subject. The 'Text' tab may hold the text version, but the image itself fails.
findings.after: alt="Apple WWDC24 email: glowing Apple logo; 'Action packed. WWDC24, June 10–14. Watch the keynote Monday June 10 at 10:00 a.m. PT, streaming from Apple Park on apple.com.' Add to calendar." or aria-describedby pointing at the Text tab panel
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content: an image of text needs a text alternative carrying the same information.

findings.where: inside the email: legal footer and grey body lines (tile 1440-01)
findings.evidence: Footer 'TM and © 2024 Apple Inc. ... If you prefer not to receive commercial email from Apple ... click here' is mid-grey at about 12px (rendered smaller in the scaled image) on black; by eye it is under 4.5:1, and the unsubscribe link is 'click here'.
findings.before: grey 12px legal text on #000; link text 'click here'
findings.after: In the source email: #a1a1a6 or lighter on black and link text 'Unsubscribe from Apple marketing email'
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) and 2.4.4 Link Purpose (applies to the email itself; in the gallery it is an image).
